items.topic: Scope boundary with theming-engine and kiosk-ux sibling items
items.context: The research is settled (17 findings), but the scaffold must draw a clean line between what it delivers and what the two downstream execute items (`command-center-theming-engine`, `command-center-kiosk-ux`) deliver. Drawing the line too tight means theming-engine starts from a blank slate; drawing it too loose means the scaffold duplicates or pre-empts sibling work. The choice drives the phase plan, testing scope, and Definition of Done.

options.label: Minimal structural scaffold
options.rationale: 6 route shells, `<div data-theme>` wrapper, empty `ThemeProvider` context, NO Fullscreen/Wake Lock hooks, NO R3F Canvas wrapper. Theming-engine brings R3F + all themes + CSS; kiosk-ux brings Fullscreen+Wake Lock hooks + auto-cycle. Cleanest boundaries but siblings start from less.

options.label: Foundation scaffold (recommended)
options.rationale: Minimal scaffold PLUS: shared R3F Canvas wrapper (`SceneCanvas.tsx`) with performance-tier hooks ready to accept per-page scenes, Fullscreen + Wake Lock hooks adapted into `ui/src/hooks/` (but not auto-invoked), one reference theme populated as a smoke-test. Theming-engine fills the 6 theme variants; kiosk-ux wires hooks into the auto-cycle + fullscreen-on-load flow. Best balance: siblings land on real seams without scope creep.

options.label: Full vertical slice
options.rationale: Foundation scaffold PLUS one complete dashboard (Mission Control): real R3F scene, real theme values, real data fetch through to gap badges. Other 5 routes are placeholders. Proves end-to-end feasibility but pre-empts theming-engine's scope for Mission Control and blurs boundaries.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different scope-boundary definition in the freeform field.

items.topic: LPBS upstream client strategy in scaffold
items.context: `execute/lpbs-command-center-dashboard-endpoints` is a separate, later item — the LPBS `/api/v1/admin/dashboard/*` handlers do not exist yet. The scaffold still needs to make decisions about its LPBS client: omit it entirely, stub it, or exercise a placeholder path. Finding 4 settled the auth pattern (Bearer token on `/api/v1/admin/*` with `requireAdminOrService`), so the wire-level contract is known even though the endpoints are missing.

options.label: No LPBS client in scaffold
options.rationale: Skip `upstream/lpbs.go` entirely; LPBS-sourced metrics always return gap-mode data from the registry. Simplest scaffold, but the sibling LPBS endpoints item has to add the client + its tests when it lands, increasing its scope.

options.label: LPBS client interface + stub implementation (recommended)
options.rationale: Author `upstream/lpbs.go` with a typed interface + an initial implementation that calls the (future) `/api/v1/admin/dashboard/*` endpoints with the Bearer token already wired. Because endpoints don't exist yet, it falls through to gap-mode cleanly on 404. When the LPBS endpoints item ships, it just needs to point the config at real URLs. Lowest rework cost; preserves tested auth plumbing.

options.label: LPBS client with mock response fixtures
options.rationale: Author the client AND include JSON fixtures that stand in for LPBS responses until real endpoints ship. Guarantees the full dashboard payload pipeline is exercisable end-to-end immediately, but creates dead code to delete when LPBS endpoints land.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different LPBS strategy in the freeform field.

items.context: The file-based JSON gap registry at `config/gap-registry.json` is loaded by the API at startup (Finding 6). This item owns the schema and the loading path, but the initial content (which metrics for which dashboards) could range from a skeleton to a fully populated catalog. The orchestration summary lists data availability per dashboard (Forge ~90% live, Broadcast ~40% live, etc.), giving us enough information to populate aggressively.

options.label: Schema-only registry
options.rationale: Ship with a near-empty registry: 1-2 sentinel entries per dashboard just to prove the loader + endpoints work. Subsequent execute items (theming-engine, plus per-dashboard items) populate real entries. Minimizes premature commitment to metric definitions that may shift.

options.label: Fully populated from orchestration summary (recommended)
options.rationale: Populate all 6 dashboards with the metrics enumerated in `orchestration-summary.md` (e.g., Forge: velocity, throughput, blocked ratio; Ledger: subscriber counts by tier, revenue, churn; etc.). Status reflects data-availability percentages (Forge heavy live, Broadcast heavy gap). Gives `/api/v1/gaps` meaningful day-1 output and provides theming-engine real metric IDs to design around. Light lock-in — entries can evolve.

options.label: Per-dashboard metadata only
options.rationale: Populate dashboard keys + display metadata (title, theme-key, description) but not individual metric entries. Leaves metric-level detail to per-dashboard items but still gives sibling items a stable dashboard list.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different gap registry scope in the freeform field.

items.context: Finding 15 settled per-dashboard `React.lazy()` code-splitting; Finding 9 settled per-page Canvas lazy mount/unmount; Finding 3 settled R3F + Recharts. The scaffold must wire the Canvas + lazy-loading infrastructure but the actual per-page scene content is theming-engine scope. The question is: does each route get an empty Canvas, a trivial placeholder scene (single mesh), or no Canvas at all in this item?

options.label: No R3F Canvas in scaffold
options.rationale: Route shells render only HTML (title + gap badges). Theming-engine adds `SceneCanvas.tsx` + all 6 scene modules. Cleanest boundary but pushes the code-split validation entirely into the theming-engine item.

options.label: Canvas wrapper + trivial per-page lazy scene (recommended)
options.rationale: Ship `SceneCanvas.tsx` that accepts a `scene` prop lazy-loaded per route. Each route imports a minimal placeholder scene (e.g. a single rotating cube with the theme's accent color) via `React.lazy()`. Proves code-splitting works, validates the per-page mount/unmount lifecycle, and gives theming-engine a drop-in replacement target. Xbox bundle-size sanity check is possible at this item's scope.

options.label: Canvas wrapper but no per-page scene modules
options.rationale: Ship `SceneCanvas.tsx` with no children; each route renders it empty. Theming-engine adds all 6 scene modules. Lighter than B but doesn't exercise `React.lazy()` per page, so the code-split seam is untested here.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different R3F scaffolding scope in the freeform field.

items.context: Finding 14 identifies Playwright as the verification tool for theme isolation (visual regression), kiosk mode, and staleness UX — but those tests are owned by the respective sibling items. The scaffold still needs to decide whether to set up Playwright config + smoke tests now, or defer entirely. Doing it now costs some scaffold overhead but removes a blocker from sibling items; deferring keeps this item tight.

options.label: No Playwright in scaffold
options.rationale: Vitest (UI) + `go test` (API) only. Kiosk-ux and theming-engine each set up their own Playwright when they need it. Tightest scaffold scope; siblings pay Playwright setup cost each.

options.label: Playwright baseline config + smoke test (recommended)
options.rationale: Install `@playwright/test`, add `ui/playwright.config.ts`, and ship ONE smoke test: `page.goto('/')` for each of the 6 routes, assert no console errors, assert `data-theme` attribute is set. No visual regression baselines, no kiosk assertions, no snapshot files. Sibling items extend the config with their own test files. Saves each sibling ~30min of setup with minimal scope creep here.

options.label: Full Playwright with per-route snapshot baseline
options.rationale: Playwright config + smoke tests + visual regression baselines captured for all 6 routes. Gives theming-engine a regression harness to test against. But baselines taken against placeholder themes will all change when theming-engine ships real themes — wasted snapshots.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different Playwright scope in the freeform field.

items.text: Verified in `templates/scenarios/react-vite/ui/package.json`: the template already ships `@tanstack/react-query`, `@vrooli/iframe-bridge`, `clsx`, `lucide-react`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`, and Radix primitives. The scaffold only needs to ADD `react-router-dom`, `recharts`, `three`, `@react-three/fiber`, `@react-three/drei`, and `framer-motion` (kiosk-ux may swap framer for a simpler primitive later). Finding 16's spatial-nav dependency (`@vrooli/iframe-bridge`) is confirmed present, so no controller-input dependency gap exists at scaffold time.

plan_updates: Round 1 created the initial `plan.md` scaffold from research conclusions and orchestration context. All 13 mandatory sections are populated. Scope, contracts, phases, testing, risks, non-goals, and Definition of Done reflect the settled research (R3F+Recharts, per-page lazy Canvas, CSS custom-property theming, file-based gap registry, per-source TTL cache, LPBS Bearer auth, iframe-bridge spatial nav). Five sections reference TBD markers tied to the round's decisions: LPBS client strategy (d2), gap-registry initial content (d3), R3F scene approach (d4), Playwright scope (d5), and the overall sibling-item scope boundary (d1) which threads through multiple sections. Readiness: problem_clarity 3, scope_defined 2, approach_solid 2, testable 2, risk_awareness 2 — sections are drafted but need d1–d5 resolved for Definition of Done to be binding.
